chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the satanic insinuations (al-waswasah), even if they were frequent, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing in it; you should say, 'La ilaha illa Allah'.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْوَسْوَسَة: Satanic insinuations or whispers of doubt
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah (declaration of faith)

ai.seo_question: How to deal with frequent satanic insinuations according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the mere presence of frequent satanic insinuations (*waswasah*) does not constitute a sin or diminish one's spiritual standing, provided the believer actively counters them with the declaration of divine unity (*La ilaha illa Allah*). This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that faith is resilient against persistent internal whispers, emphasizing the importance of conscious verbal response over passive endurance of doubt. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining spiritual composure during prolonged periods of distraction or temptation.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Muhammad Bin Humran who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the (Satanic) insinuations and if it was frequent. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing in it. You should be saying, ‘لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ’ ‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Muhammad ibn Humran who has said the following:
“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘What if temptation (soul’s tale telling) becomes a great deal.’ The Imam said, ‘There is nothing in it. Say, ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah.’”
